subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: Jacquard's Loom: Programmable Machines
description: A fast breakdown of Jacquard's Loom: Programmable Machines for builders.

hook.text: In 1804, Joseph-Marie Jacquard used punched cards to control a loom. The pattern lived on the cards, not the weaver.

buildup.text: Holes in the cards let hooks pass through to lift specific threads. No holes meant the threads stayed down.

discovery.text: Complex patterns that took days to set up could now repeat endlessly. Change the cards, change the pattern.

twist.text: Workers rioted and smashed the looms, fearing job losses. The Luddite revolt was one of history's first automation panics.

climax.text: Babbage borrowed Jacquard's punched card idea for his Analytical Engine. Looms inspired computing.

punchline.text: Punched holes told thread what to do. Programming started with fabric.

quiz.question: How did Jacquard's punched cards influence computing?
options: They powered the first electric looms that replaced steam engines
Babbage adopted the punched card concept for his Analytical Engine
They were used directly as memory storage in early computers
